title: The wholesale drug licence: requirement, annual renewal, per-location licensing, reported information and inspection
rule_summary: Under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 36A, except as provided in s. 35, no person shall engage in the sale, distribution or delivery, at wholesale, of drugs or medicines within the commonwealth without a license. Under s. 36B the Board issues the licence on application and payment of an annual license fee, only if satisfied that the applicant is actually engaged in and carrying on the wholesale business; the licence shall be renewed on or before December first of each year on payment of the fee; and a person engaged in the wholesale drug business at more than one location shall obtain a licence for each location. Under s. 36C no person shall use the words wholesale druggist or words of similar import without first being licensed, and the agents of the Board have authority, during business hours, to inspect and investigate all wholesale dealers in drugs or medicines and shall report violations to the Board. Under 247 CMR 7.02(1) every wholesale distributor located in Massachusetts that engages in wholesale distribution of prescription drugs shall be licensed by the Board before engaging in it; under 7.02(2) applications are made on Board forms, completely filled out and signed by each applicant under oath before a notary public, and the Board shall not consider an application within 15 days after its filing or one improperly completed or not accompanied by the appropriate fees; under 7.02(3) the Board may require a hearing on the merits with seven days notice by certified mail; under 7.02(4) a person engaged in the wholesale drug business at more than one location obtains a licence for each location. Under 7.02(5) the Board requires, as part of initial licensing and of any renewal: the name, full business address and telephone number of the applicant or licensee; all trade or business names used; addresses, telephone numbers and contact persons for each facility used for storage, handling and distribution of prescription drugs; and the type of ownership or operation, with the names of the person, partners, corporate officers and directors (with corporate names, state of incorporation and any parent company) or sole proprietor as applicable, and an indication whether controlled substances, legend drugs or over-the-counter drugs will be distributed with a statement of the types of drugs. Under 7.02(6) changes in any information in 247 CMR 7.02(5) shall be submitted to the Board in writing within 30 days after such change. Under 7.02(9), as a condition for receiving and retaining a licence, the licensee shall require each person employed in any prescription drug wholesale distribution activity to have education, training and experience sufficient to perform the assigned functions so that drug product quality, safety and security will at all times be maintained as required by law. Under 7.03(1) the agents of the Board may inspect and investigate all wholesale drug distributors and shall report violations to the Board, and shall provide the licensee a copy of the inspection report within 15 days of the inspection. Under 7.04(9)(b) wholesale drug distributors shall permit the agents of the Board and authorized federal, state and local law enforcement officials to enter and inspect their premises and delivery vehicles, and to audit their records and written operating procedures, at reasonable times and in a reasonable manner, to the extent authorized by law.
exam_relevance: Tests that the wholesale licence runs on an annual December renewal unlike a pharmacy licence, attaches to each location, and carries its own inspection and reporting terms.

exceptions: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 36A applies except as otherwise provided in s. 35.
common_confusions: The wholesale licence is renewed each year, on or before December first; a Drug Store Pharmacy licence runs to December 31 of an odd-numbered year.
One licence does not cover several locations.
Statutory inspection authority under s. 36C is stated for business hours; 247 CMR 7.04(9)(b) speaks of reasonable times and a reasonable manner.
